These new Phase 3 targets were determined following an extensive review and evaluation of the Phase 2 drill results, as well as the recently completed Terēan Shear-Wave Seismic Geophysical Survey (see previous press releases dated

Numerous polymetallic zones were encountered during the Phase 2 program. The drill holes encountered highly fractured rock with abundant clay alteration and brightly coloured orange and red oxide minerals and decalcification. Assay results confirmed that the area surrounding discovery drill hole GMST-4 is mineralized and geologically complex, which prompted the Company to conduct the Terēan seismic survey in order to gain a more complete understanding of fracturing, alteration, and lithology and to further evaluate the structural interpretations derived from the Phase 2 drill program. The results of the seismic survey were remarkably consistent with the logged stratigraphy encountered during the Phase 2 drill program.

The shear-wave seismic survey identified several interpreted low-velocity zones and structural discontinuities across the surveyed area. Certain anomalies occur in proximity to geological features previously encountered in drilling, including zones of decalcification, alteration and mineralization associated with discovery hole GMST-4. Therefore, the Company interprets the Terēan survey low-velocity zones as high-quality targets for Phase 3 drilling. The Company believes these interpretations provide additional geological context for selecting Phase 3 drill targets. However, the presence, grade and continuity of mineralization within the newly identified targets can only be established through drilling and analytical testing.

Glenstar has identified nine proposed collar locations for reverse circulation ("RC") drilling at the Green Monster Project, based on the integration of geological observations, previous drill results and the recently completed Terēan shear-wave seismic survey.

The proposed Phase 3 program comprises ten RC drill holes from nine collars, subject to final drill planning and regulatory authorization. The proposed holes are designed to investigate interpreted low-velocity zones, structural discontinuities and geological features that may be associated with alteration and mineralization encountered during earlier exploration programs.

Proposed Phase 3 reverse circulation drill program at Glenstar Minerals Inc.'s Green Monster Project in Clark County, Nevada. Green stars mark nine proposed collar locations for ten drill holes. GMST-14 and GMST-14A share a collar, with GMST-14A planned to be drilled eastward at a 70° angle.

The seismic survey identified a series of interpreted structural features and localized velocity anomalies across four survey lines. These include lateral changes and offsets in shear-wave velocity boundaries, as well as discrete low-velocity intervals that may reflect fractured, altered or dissolution-affected rock.

Proposed holes GMST-12 through GMST-20, including GMST-14A, will evaluate selected geophysical anomalies and investigate the potential lateral and vertical extent of prospective geological features. GMST-14 and GMST-14A will be drilled from the same collar. GMST-14A will be angled east at 70 degrees.

The Phase 3 program is intended to further refine the Company's understanding of the structural and geological controls on mineralization at Green Monster. The geophysical interpretations remain preliminary, and there can be no assurance that the identified anomalies correspond to mineralization.
The Company is preparing the necessary application to the United States Bureau of Land Management (
) for the proposed Phase 3 drilling program. Drilling will be subject to receipt of all required approvals and authorizations.

Project Manager and Qualified Person Bob Marvin, commented,

"Our proposed Phase 3 drilling program represents an important step in advancing our geological understanding of the Green Monster Project. By integrating the results of our earlier drilling programs with the recently completed shear-wave seismic survey, we have identified nine targets designed to investigate interpreted structural features and potential extensions of the alteration and mineralization encountered in discovery hole GMST-4.

"The seismic survey has provided valuable insight into the distribution of interpreted low-velocity zones and structural discontinuities across the project area. We believe these findings will help us prioritize drilling and evaluate the potential continuity of the geological features identified to date," added Marvin.

The Green Monster Property is comprised of 35 federal lode claims covering ~700 acres located in Clark County, Nevada, on the west-trending spur of the Spring Mountains and is approximately 40 miles southwest of Las Vegas. Until the recent drill programs conducted in May of 2025 and February of 2026, no drilling was ever conducted on the property. The Company's previous identification of robust nickel-copper with anomalous cobalt from sampling work done in 2022 indicated that several targets were ideal for shallow RC drilling (see press releases dated May 28, 2025, and July 16, 2025).

Glenstar acquired the Green Monster Property and conducted initial groundwork in 2022 that included reconnaissance geologic mapping, surface rock sampling, soil sampling, and a drone magnetic survey. Channel sampling across the exposed back of a raise off the main shaft returned 1.18 meters of 3.77% Cu (Copper), 3.06% Ni (Nickel), 0.21% Co (Cobalt) and 6.83% Zn (Zinc). These values are well in excess of select dump samples from historical underground workings and represent in-place, vein-style mineralization. Sampling of oxide and sulfide bearing boulders directly downhill of the patented workings has confirmed the presence of very high zinc (>10%) and silver (>200ppm), as well as copper, uranium, and lead. (Sampling results provided above were previously published in the Green Monster Project NI 43-101 Technical Report dated June 20, 2023, Section 7.5).

Glenstar is a mineral exploration company with a focus on polymetallic minerals. These elements are classified as critical minerals and are essential in the manufacturing of sophisticated electronics and other vital energy technologies. The Company's mission is to leverage its knowledge and connections to explore, acquire, and develop critical mineral and energy metal properties throughout the world.
